__inputs.name: DS_PROM
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: The Prometheus data source holding the generator metrics

title: Generator — B-Infohub local bridge
description: Everything the local RS-485 bridge reads off the GC-1032, including the 32 individual alarm bits and the per-leg and cumulative readings the EnergyTrak cloud never carried. The existing cloud dashboard is unaffected.

panels.title: UTILITY
panels.description: Utility feed as the generator's own controller sees it — not a ping test.

panels.title: MODE
panels.description: The physical AUTO / MANUAL / OFF switch on the GC-1032 panel.

panels.title: WILL IT START?
panels.description: The question the MODE panel only implies. Anything other than AUTO means the generator will NOT respond to a utility failure, and nothing else on this dashboard would look wrong.

panels.title: EXERCISE
panels.description: Alerting suppresses on this, which is why the weekly test does not page you.

panels.title: LAST DATA PUSHED
panels.description: Wall-clock time of the newest sample Grafana actually holds.

panels.title: PUSH AGE (real)
panels.description:
WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS 'local data age'.

generator_bridge_bus_age_seconds is a value the bridge REPORTS and Home Assistant PUSHES. If the push stops -- HA down, automation disabled, expired Grafana key -- the last pushed value simply freezes. It would have sat at '9 s' forever while nothing arrived, which is the most misleading thing an indicator can do.

This is computed by Prometheus from the sample's own timestamp, so it counts up the moment delivery stops, no matter why.

panels.title: PUSHES / MIN
panels.description: Expect 2 — the automation fires every 30s. Zero means delivery has stopped.

panels.title: Generator → bridge age
panels.description: Seconds since a Modbus register last arrived at the bridge. This is the RS-485 link only. For whether the data is reaching Grafana at all, read PUSH AGE — this value is itself pushed, so it freezes if delivery stops.

panels.title: Data freshness: local bridge vs EnergyTrak cloud
panels.description: The reason the bridge exists. Local age is single-digit seconds; the cloud feed is typically minutes behind. Both are plotted on one axis so the gap is the shape of the graph rather than a number you have to remember.

panels.title: Engine speed
panels.description: 3600 RPM is 60Hz. A weekly exercise sits near 2800 through low-speed warm-up.

panels.title: Battery voltage
panels.description: The single best predictor of a failed start. ~12.6V at rest, ~13.5V while the alternator is charging. A deep sag during cranking that does not recover is the warning you get in advance of a no-start.

panels.title: Coolant temperature
panels.description: Local-only: the cloud never carried this.

panels.title: Generator frequency
panels.description: 60Hz under load. ~46.7Hz during low-speed warm-up is normal on this unit.

panels.title: Cumulative energy
panels.description: Local-only lifetime counters. Never exposed by the cloud.

panels.title: Utility voltage
panels.description: grid_voltage is the line-to-line figure, matching what the EnergyTrak cloud reports under the same name. The per-leg readings are local-only.

panels.title: Alarm history
panels.description: Every discrete alarm the controller exposes, one series each. The cloud collapsed all of these into a single 'fault' string. Only bits that have been asserted in the window are drawn, so an empty panel means a clean generator.

panels.title: Source and reachability
panels.description: Three separate facts that a single 'online' indicator would blur. Reachable off means the ESP32 is not answering. Bus healthy off means it is answering while the generator has gone quiet on RS-485 — a different fault, at a different end of the install.

panels.title: Run state
panels.description: The exercise bits are why a weekly test does not page you: the alerting suppresses on these, and a start is only surprising when both are clear and the grid is healthy.

options.content:
### Not shown, on purpose

This dashboard only plots readings this generator actually produces. A panel
that can only ever say **No data** is worse than no panel — it looks like a
fault in the monitoring.

**Sensors not fitted on this unit.** These registers answer `0xFFFF`, the
controller's code for *sensor not present*, so nothing is published for them
and no series exists:

`oil_pressure` · `fuel_level` · `fuel_volume` · `generator_l3_*` ·
`utility_l3_*` · L3 currents and per-phase power

The L3 readings are absent because this is a **split-phase** machine — it has
L1 and L2 and there is no third phase to measure.

**Bits that are asserted but meaningless here.** Nine discrete inputs sit
permanently at 1 because nothing is wired to them: `fuel_theft`,
`water_level_switch`, `low_fuel_level`, `fuel_cap_open_circuit`,
`oil_pressure_open_circuit`, `extended_over_load_trip`, `maintenance_required`,
and the two `gen_l3_phase_*` alarms. They are pushed to Prometheus so the data
is there if hardware is ever added, but they are deliberately excluded from the
alarm timeline and from every alert rule. Counting them is what once pinned the
`fault` sensor ON permanently.

**If a sensor is added later** it appears on its own: the push discovers fields
rather than listing them, so the series starts flowing the moment the bridge
reports a real value. Only the panel has to be added here.
